g0.rationale: §2.2 five-step test. Step 1: authoritative directions located (aggregated retailer copy, moderate confidence — recorded as a limitation). Step 2: mode (1) 'Intensivpflege — ins nasse Haar einmassieren, 3-5 Minuten einwirken lassen, mit warmem Wasser ausspülen' has a stated contact time and a rinse and is framed as the post-wash intensive mode; modes (2) and (3) are explicitly 'nicht ausspülen' and fail the rinse conjunct outright. Step 3: exactly one mode qualifies → mode-scoped classification with a multi_use envelope. Charter F1 names Isana 3in1 as a live boundary case that is eligible mode-scoped.

careDirection.evidenceScope: Formula-only, above-tail ranks 1–15; comparative care emphasis, never an assertion about a user's protein state (G6).
careDirection.rationale: Two distinct qualifying R5 species sit above the tail, one of them at rank 6 (inside the first eight above-tail ranks), so the material-R5 test is satisfied on both of its legs. The `balanced` second conjunct is then met by S3. As with #04 the value is earned through the lipid leg rather than a humectant cluster — this formula contains no glycerin at all and only one above-tail humectant. E2 ceiling: comparative emphasis, not a delivered outcome.
evidenceSignals: HYDROLYZED MILK PROTEIN (rank 6) — qualifying R5 species above the tail, within the first eight above-tail ranks
LAURDIMONIUM HYDROXYPROPYL HYDROLYZED WHEAT PROTEIN (rank 10) — second distinct qualifying R5 species; lexicon family 5a explicitly includes cationised protein derivatives
S3 lipid leg: six distinct non-fatty-alcohol lipids above the tail
PANTHENOL (rank 11) — the sole above-tail humectant; no glycerin in the formula at all
CITRIC ACID (rank 15) — the Stearamidopropyl Dimethylamine neutraliser (C3), never an active
careDirection.derivation: §9.3 material-R5 test satisfied on leg (a) (two distinct species above the tail) and independently on leg (b) (a single qualifying species at above-tail rank 6, inside the first eight). Then the `balanced` test: material R5 route AND (humectant cluster OR S3). Humectant cluster fails at one member; S3 succeeds. → `balanced`.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `balanced`: both conjuncts of §9.3's operational test hold.

`protein` does not apply: it shares the first conjunct with `balanced`, and `balanced` is selected because the second conjunct also holds. Note that on the substance — two proteins, one cationised, one at rank 6, against a single humectant — `protein` is arguably the more faithful description, and it is only the S3 lipid leg that pushes this to `balanced`. This is the clearest instance in the cohort of AP-04-BALANCEDBAR.
`moisture` does not apply: a two-species R5 route above the tail is a protein-film route, which the `moisture` definition excludes.
counterSignals: D4 heavy-protein-payload counter-signal FIRES (two distinct R5 species above the tail), binding confidence to `moderate`.
The humectant side of a value literally named `balanced` is a single panthenol. The value does not describe this formula's balance; it describes the test's structure.
limitations: INCI discloses no molecular weight; the route supports 'a protein film route is present' and nothing more.
Banned vocabulary observed: no 'protein overload' language.

adjudicationPoints.title: §2.1's 'after cleansing' conjunct is inferred, not stated, on several multi-use products
adjudicationPoints.body: Isana's mask mode reads 'ins nasse Haar einmassieren, 3-5 Minuten einwirken lassen, mit warmem Wasser ausspülen'. It never says 'nach der Haarwäsche'. I ruled the mode qualifying because it is labelled Intensivpflege, is on wet hair, and stands in explicit contrast to modes 2 and 3 which are on towel-dry and dry hair — but that is an inference chain, not a directions fact, and it is exactly the kind of step §2.2 step 5 tells reviewers not to guess at. Combined with AP-G0-PLACEMENT (the unstated 'lengths and ends' conjunct), this means G0 eligibility on multi-use products currently rests on reviewer inference more often than the standard's language suggests. Candidate fix: §2.2 should say which conjuncts may be inferred from mode labelling and which must be verbatim.

adjudicationPoints.title: The D5 guard's 'two further distinct humectants' phrasing assumes glycerin is present
adjudicationPoints.body: D5's ruled wording is 'glycerin alone never qualifies — moisture requires at least two FURTHER distinct humectants above the tail'. §9.5.3 operationalizes this as '≥3 distinct, of which ≥2 are not glycerin'. Two cohort formulas (#05, #12) contain no glycerin at all, so the operationalization reads as 'any 3 distinct humectants', which is a materially easier bar than the ruled sentence implies for a glycerin-containing formula. It did not change an answer in this cohort (#05 has one humectant, #12 has two), but it is a latent inconsistency that a glycerin-free product with three humectants would expose.
